verdict.rationale: Solid's own docs state it compiles templates to real DOM nodes and updates them with fine-grained reactions instead of a Virtual DOM, so only dependent code reruns. The compiler is wired in through babel-preset-solid. Community users independently confirm the DOM performance, including one report of a rebuilt player that was 4x smaller and 50x faster. missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the compiler's output and transformation details.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a compiler to translate my components into efficient, surgical DOM updates instead of writing manual diffing code

citations.quote: Instead of using a Virtual DOM, it compiles its templates to real DOM nodes and updates them with fine-grained reactions.
The easiest way to get set up is to add `babel-preset-solid` to your `.babelrc`, babel config for webpack, or rollup configuration
when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it will rerun.
